intent: Make the whole attachment card one click target that opens or previews the file, while its actions stay separately clickable.
typical_uses: Opening a preview dialog for the attached file
Linking the whole card to the file, rendered as a link

dont_use_when.situation: A separate action on the attachment, such as remove
A clickable control that is not an attachment card

invariants.text: The trigger is absolutely positioned over the whole of its Attachment (`inset: 0`, `z-index: 10`), so a click on the preview, the title or the description lands on it, while AttachmentActions (`z-index: 20`) stay above it.
The trigger renders no text of its own, so the `aria-label` passed to it names the rendered button or link.
Without `render` it renders a `<button>` with `type="button"` unless a `type` is given; with `render` no `type` is added.

anti_patterns.dont: Wrap the whole Attachment in a link or a button to make it clickable
anti_patterns.do_instead: Put an AttachmentTrigger inside it, rendered as a link with `render` when it navigates, so AttachmentActions stay separate controls

a11y.by: attachment.test.tsx asserts that AttachmentTrigger renders a BUTTON with type "button", and that with `render={<a href="..." />}` and aria-label="Open report.pdf" it is found by role "link" with that accessible name

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (AttachmentTrigger passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

good.title: The whole card as a link to the file

bad.title: Text children as the trigger's name
bad.why: The trigger is an overlay covering the whole card, so its text is drawn over the title and preview; name it with `aria-label` and leave it empty.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (AttachmentTrigger passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.
